name: tier1_combined_review
_comment: THE COMBINED SCENE — one room, both surfaces, judged together.
Both tier-one lanes finished soloing against scenes built for their own question, and each
lane's frames were half debug colour to the other's eye: three floor rounds spent most of
their flip list on the wall lane's magenta mocks, and one seat read those mocks as the
FLOOR's lighting. This spec exists so that neither surface is judged again in a frame the
other one has not really been laid into.
GEOMETRY IS tier1_wall_review's, UNCHANGED, and deliberately so. That spec was built to put
all four of §3's contexts in one frame — south reveals at more than one range, a chokepoint
between two masses, inner and outer corners, and wall seen at a glance rather than only up
close — and it is the only review geometry that also carries a non-zero traffic field
(spine 18 / routes 25). Re-deriving a room would have thrown that away to no purpose, and
§9e records what a traffic-dead scene costs: every traffic-keyed system in it is untested
while looking tested.
WHAT MOVES IS THE STATION, and it moves for the FLOOR's law rather than for the wall's.
Round 24 ruled that stations for traffic-keyed questions are SAMPLED FROM THE POLYLINE: the
player stands ON the route, and the route AHEAD lies inside the lamp's delivered pool. The
wall gate's station at (8,15) has route strength ZERO — it was chosen when the floor was not
the question — so a combined round taken there would judge the floor's whole traffic system
on ground the level's own graph says nobody walks. That is round 23's VOID-FOR-STATION
failure, and taking the wall lane's station unexamined would have reproduced it silently.
THE STATION IS (6,12), read off this scene's own route-strength map, where the route
crosses room A on its way from the chokepoint mouth to the south-west alcove. From here:
the route AHEAD runs (5,13) (4,14) (3,15), all inside the delivered reach
the masses' SOUTH FACE row (y=11) stands 1 tile north — the range §6.5 is now scoped
to, and at n=11 cells rather than the wall gate station's n=1
the ISLAND at (5,15) is 3.2 tiles south-west: four outer corners, the case §3's
two-plane rule is hardest on, because an outer corner is where a wall stops
the CHOKEPOINT MOUTH at (8,11) is a one-wide doorway with jambs at (7,11) and (9,11) —
four inner corners — 2.2 tiles away
room A's east end and the mass beyond it run out past the delivered reach of about four
tiles, because a scene where every wall is legible is not the game (§6.2's arc)
⚠ THE STATION IS ONE TILE EAST OF THE ROUTE'S PEAK, AND THAT TILE IS THE WHOLE REASON.
The peak sits at (5,13) and the first capture was taken there. At x=5 the camera's left
edge falls at tile −0.86, i.e. OUTSIDE THE MAP, and the engine fills out-of-map ground with
a flat 77-grey that the light rig never touches: measured on that frame, a 55px column at
exactly (77,77,77) with a standard deviation of 0.00, running the full height of the
dungeon view, against a void of 3.2 beside it. It is the brightest thing in the frame after
the lamp pool and it has a ruled straight edge. Any seat would have culled the frame for it
and the cull would have been about the harness. (6,12) is still on the route — strength one
band below the peak — and puts the map edge off-frame. The grey itself is engine behaviour
and is reported rather than fixed here: it is neither floor nor wall material.
_station_trail: (5,13) — route peak. REJECTED: put the map edge in frame (see above).
_void_note: THE VOID IS NOT IN THIS FILE. Which cells are void is a wall-family question and it is set
per capture — see tools/tier1_floors/capture_combined.sh and the --void-ring it passes, and
the flag's own documentation on Tier1BoundaryWall.Apply for why that is a command-line
decision rather than a manifest edit.
_legibility: Wall faces are probed at the FLOOR cell they stand over, exactly as the wall gate scene
probed them: the probe reads a cell's delivered luminance, and a face is not a cell.
Nothing east of x=10 or south of y=20 is declared — at this camera it is outside the frame,
and a still cannot check ground it does not contain.

legibility.why: 1 tile — the floor at the foot of the masses' south face. The standing case, and the ground §6.5's stack is a relationship against
2.8 tiles — the route ahead. If this is dark the station is wrong and the floor's traffic systems are being judged unlit, which is round 23's failure
3 tiles — the floor beside the island, which is what its outer corners are read against
5.1 tiles — room A's east end, past the delivered reach of about four. The arc is part of the distribution and a scene where everything is lit is not the game
5.4 tiles — the chokepoint deep inside the mass, in frame and unlit

_carve_note: Row 15 is carved in two pieces either side of x=5, which leaves ONE CELL STANDING at (5,15).
That is the island: floor on all four sides and on all four diagonals, so it is the only
geometry in any review scene that puts four OUTER corners in frame. Inherited unchanged from
tier1_wall_review — every rect in this list is that spec's, byte for byte, so a comparison
between the two scenes is a comparison of stations and of nothing else.
